column1: # ZAP baseline triage (Phase 11, task 9).
# One line per rule ZAP raises that this application will not act on, with the
# reason. IGNORE means "we looked at this and it does not apply here"; anything
# absent from this file is reported and has to be triaged before it can be
# added, which is the point of keeping the file short.
# Format: <rule id>
# Reference: https://www.zaproxy.org/docs/docker/baseline-scan/
# 10015 — no Cache-Control on some responses. Laravel sets `no-cache` on
# anything session-bearing; the pages ZAP reaches unauthenticated are a shell
# with no secret in it. The bytes worth caching are the hashed asset filenames,
# which are immutable by construction.

column3: Static asset responses are content-hashed and hold no user data.

column1: # 10027 — information disclosure in a suspicious comment. The bundle carries
# the word "password" in field labels and in the strength meter's wordlist.

column3: Matches UI copy in the bundle, not a leaked implementation detail.

column1: # 10109 — modern web application. An informational alert saying the crawler
# found little to crawl, which is what a client-rendered SPA looks like.

column3: Informational: Inertia renders client-side, so there is nothing to spider.

column1: # 10202 — absent anti-CSRF tokens on forms. There are no HTML forms: every
# write is an XHR carrying the X-XSRF-TOKEN header that Laravel's middleware
# checks, which ZAP's form scanner cannot see.

column3: CSRF is enforced on the XHR header, not on a hidden form field.

column1: # 90005 — Sec-Fetch metadata not enforced server-side. The controls that do
# this job here are `frame-ancestors 'none'`, SameSite cookies and COOP/COEP.

column3: Covered by frame-ancestors, SameSite and cross-origin isolation.
